title: Small trees in the primary street setback area (Table 1.2a)
text: Tree Canopy. C1.2.4 A minimum number of trees to be planted in accordance with Tables 1.2a and provided with the required deep soil area per tree in accordance with Table 1.2b. Table 1.2a Minimum tree provisions. Grouped dwellings, primary street setback: Where the primary street setback is 1.5m or greater: - Frontages less than 20m: 1 small tree in the primary street setback area; or - Frontages 20m or greater: 1 small tree in the primary street setback area per 10m of frontage(2). Trees required within the street setback area are in addition to trees required per dwelling and where providing a secondary private open space. 2 Frontage to be rounded down to the nearest 10m. Tree provisions exclude ancillary dwellings.

replaces.note: Part B: one tree per dwelling, no street-setback tree

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 3 - Grouped Dwellings.pdf

verified.note: Values (1 tree under 20m frontage, 1 per 10m rounded down at 20m or more) check. Table 1.2a 'Where the primary street setback is 1.5m or greater' does not say whether this is the setback provided or the setback required by Table 3.3a, nor whether 'frontage' is the frontage of the parent lot of the grouped development.

notes: Content twin of Chapter 2 C1.2.3, renumbered C1.2.4 in Chapter 3 (p11); test unchanged. Applies where the primary street setback is 1.5 m or greater (rule condition; read as the setback provided). Frontage under 20 m: 1 small tree; 20 m or more: 1 per 10 m rounded down (table-1.2a). Street setback trees are additional to the per-dwelling trees (C1.2.4-r1) and the C1.1.4 tree. Frontage is the lot frontage of the development. Excludes ancillary dwellings and R100-SL.
